given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Loans are lent on 03-02 and the clock is moved to 03-17, so their dueOn of 03-16 is before today.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The loans start with no reminders, and the job is expected to send for them.

then.why: fakeNotifications.sent must contain exactly two reminders, so skipping the call would fail.
Each sent item must have the right memberId, loanId and dueOn, and the two members differ.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The reminders table must hold sent_on 2026-03-17, which is today and differs from dueOn 03-16.
B3 checks that a refused loan is not recorded. mutants.json says that covers this part.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, and loan1 must be sent only once.
loan2 is overdue and then returned before the job runs.
loan3 is due exactly 03-17, which is today, so it covers the boundary where dueOn equals today.

then.why: toMatchObject on an array also checks its length, so sent must be exactly [loan1]. A second send, a returned loan or a not-yet-due loan would each fail it.

given.why: fakeNotifications.refuseFor(loan1, ...) makes the fake return a refusal for loan1.
Only a refusal with a 503 reason is set up. No test makes the API unreachable, and B5 doesn't either.

then.why: The reminders table must hold only loan2's row.
toContainEqual matches the exact level and event.
The fields must equal exactly loan1 and the fake's reason string.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan2 must still be sent after loan1 is refused. loan1 is the earlier-dated loan.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs to completion.

then.why: The last log entry must equal the exact level and event.
fields must equal { sent: 2, failed: 1 }, so each count is pinned to a different value.

given.why: The test calls the real client with a reminder.

then.why: The method and the pathname are asserted on the captured request.

then.part: with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The content-type and the full body are compared with toEqual.
202, 200 and 204 are each accepted, so a check for 200 only would fail.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives kind refused and a reason containing "400".

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: No test fails the connection, so removing the catch or changing the unreachable reason would pass.
